_meta.indication: Treatment of thrombocytopenia in patients with chronic immune (idiopathic) thrombocytopenic purpura who have had an insufficient response to corticosteroids, immunoglobulins, or splenectomy.

pivotal_trials.design: Double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled parallel-group trial; eltrombopag 50 mg (dose increase up to 75 mg permitted) vs placebo for up to 6 weeks, randomized 2:1.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with chronic ITP who had failed or relapsed after at least one prior ITP therapy and had baseline platelet counts <30 x 10^9/L.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of subjects with a platelet count >=50 Gi/L after up to 42 days of dosing (treatment responders).
pivotal_trials.result: 59% of eltrombopag subjects reached platelet count >=50 Gi/L on Day 43 vs 16% placebo; odds ratio 9.6 (95% CI 3.3, 27.9); p<0.001.

pivotal_trials.design: Global, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, dose-ranging study (eltrombopag 30 mg, 50 mg, 75 mg vs placebo), randomized 1:1:1:1.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with chronic ITP and platelet counts <30 Gi/L.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of subjects with a platelet count >=50 Gi/L after up to 42 days of dosing.
pivotal_trials.result: Dose-dependent increase in responders: 11% of placebo attained platelet count >=50 Gi/L on Day 43 vs 70-80% on eltrombopag 50 mg and 75 mg; odds ratio to placebo statistically significant in 50 mg and 75 mg arms (p<0.001).

key_safety: Boxed warning for hepatotoxicity. Most common adverse reactions were nausea, vomiting, menorrhagia, myalgia, paresthesia and cataracts (occurring in 3 to 6% of eltrombopag patients). Cataracts developed or worsened in 5% of eltrombopag 50 mg patients vs 3% of placebo. Transient platelet decreases below baseline after discontinuation occurred in 10% of eltrombopag vs 6% of placebo.
target_moa: Eltrombopag is an orally bioavailable small-molecule thrombopoietin (TPO) receptor agonist that interacts with the transmembrane domain of the human TPO receptor (cMpl), initiating signaling that induces proliferation and differentiation of megakaryocytes and increased platelet production.

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: RISK FOR HEPATOTOXICITY. PROMACTA may cause hepatotoxicity; measure ALT, AST, and bilirubin prior to initiation and during treatment; discontinue if ALT >=3x ULN and progressive, persistent >=4 weeks, accompanied by increased direct bilirubin, or clinical symptoms of liver injury.

rems.type: A REMS is required (PROMACTA CARES restricted distribution program) consisting of a Medication Guide, elements to assure safe use, an implementation system, and a timetable for assessment, to ensure the benefits outweigh the risks of hepatotoxicity, bone marrow fibrosis, worsened thrombocytopenia/hemorrhage after cessation, thromboembolic complications, and malignancies.

requirement.text: Conduct a milk-only lactation study in the subset of women enrolled in the pregnancy registry who choose to breastfeed, to detect presence and concentration of Promacta in breast milk and effects on breastfeeding infants.

citations.quote: 4. To conduct a milk-only lactation study in the subset of women enrolled in the pregnancy registry that choose to breastfeed their infants. This study will be designed to detect the presence and concentration of Promacta® (eltrombopag) Tablets in breast milk and any effects on milk production and composition. The study will include a symptom diary for mothers to record any adverse effects in the breastfeeding infants.

The protocol for this trial was previously submitted to FDA and the study is currently active. The protocol will be modified to include performance of bone marrow examinations prior to the initiation of Promacta® (eltrombopag) Tablets, following 12 months of Promacta® (eltrombopag) Tablets therapy as well as following the completion of 24 months of Promacta® (eltrombopag) Tablets therapy; enrollment will

continue until these data are obtained from at least 150 patients. An interim report will contain, in addition to any other items, results of bone marrow evaluations for patients who have completed bone marrow evaluations at baseline and following 12 months of Promacta® (eltrombopag) Tablets therapy.
